source.repro: node website/scripts/readpath-bench.ts — a local node server, headless Chrome, both arms read the same bytes inside a WORKER (the realm an adapter reads in), interleaved, min of 15. Run it three times and read the ratio, not the milliseconds.
source.notes: Absolute ms are load-sensitive: three runs at load averages between ~4 and ~31 disagreed by 3x on the milliseconds and agreed on every ratio to within 0.2x, and on the crossover exactly. The sub-10MB direction is the tight one — all three runs put it between 0.53x and 0.91x. Above the crossover the spread is wider (0.94x-1.36x at 100MB), so read that half as 'a wash to a modest win', not as a number. Measured against generic-filehandle2 2.3.1, whose two paths this bench copies verbatim; `Response.prototype.bytes` exists in this Chrome, so the plain arm is one native call rather than the arrayBuffer fallback.
